TDMM models longitudinal outcomes using time-varying coefficient functions and a subject-specific random intercept. The [reference index](../reference/index.html) documents fitting, priors, computational controls, plotting, diagnostics, and data checks. The package's [Sweave Getting Started vignette](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/blob/main/vignettes/getting-started.Rnw) gives the full introductory workflow.

New fits use cubic B-splines (degree 3, order 4), `n_basis = 8` by default, and a second-order coefficient-difference penalty. `n_basis` directly specifies the number of basis functions. The `nknots` argument is retained for compatibility with older calls; use `n_basis` for new work. Family-specific priors can be inspected with `tdmm.priors()`.

For documentation of the archived v0.1.0 implementation, see the [historical V1 tutorial](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/blob/main/TDMM_tutorial.pdf). Its spline defaults and workflow should not be applied to current V2 fits.
